_readme: The six WhatsApp templates this app sends. Transactional notifications fire
outside the 24h customer service window, where Meta rejects free-form text with
error 131047 — only an approved template works.
TO CREATE: python manage.py create_wa_templates   (reads this file, POSTs each to
the Graph message_templates endpoint). Requires WHATSAPP_WABA_ID in .env.
Then: python manage.py check_wa_templates        (track review; explains rejections)
PARAMETERS ARE POSITIONAL, and that is forced by Meta, not preference. Creating a
NAMED template that has variables through the Graph API does not work: supplying
'example' fails with subcode 2388043 ('component of type BODY is missing expected
field(s) (example)'), and omitting it creates the template only for it to come
back REJECTED / INVALID_FORMAT. POSITIONAL with example.body_text is accepted.
Verified live against WABA 1384537200534046, 2026-10.
So the body uses {{1}}..{{N}}. 'parameters' below is the ordered contract: index i
is {{i+1}} in the body. The 'param_name' values are NOT sent to Meta — they are how
notifications/services.py:send_typed() names things when it builds a params dict, and
the send order is derived from THIS list, never from Python dict order.
TO ENABLE: put the approved template name in .env, e.g.
WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_INSTALLMENT_REMINDER=samana_installment_due
A blank value makes that notification fail with a log message naming the setting.
sub_category must be one of the three this account accepts — ORDER_DETAILS,
ORDER_STATUS, RICH_ORDER_STATUS. But ORDER_STATUS is itself unusable here: it refuses
with subcode 2388210 ('There should not be title or button(s) in an order status
template'), so all six use ORDER_DETAILS.

_notes: allow_category_change=false: if Meta decides a template is actually promotional we
WANT a REJECTED(INCORRECT_CATEGORY) we can see and fix, not a silent reclassification
to MARKETING — which would change pricing and imply an opt-in we never collected.
All six are unambiguously transactional, so let a mismatch surface.

templates.body: Dear {{1}}, your payment of Rs {{2}} has been received. Booking: {{3}}. Remaining balance: Rs {{4}}. Next installment: {{5}}. Thank you. — Samana Builders & Developers
templates.notes: next_installment is omitted entirely when nothing is outstanding, so {{5}} may be absent.

templates.body: Dear {{1}}, your booking {{2}} has been created. Plot {{3}} at {{4}}. Total amount: Rs {{5}}. — Samana Builders & Developers
Dear {{1}}, your booking {{2}} has been confirmed. Plot {{3}} at {{4}}. Total amount: Rs {{5}}. Please proceed with the down payment as per your payment plan. — Samana Builders & Developers
templates.notes: Sent from core/views.py booking_confirm_view, not services.py.

templates.body: Dear {{1}}, this is a reminder that installment #{{2}} of Rs {{3}} is due on {{4}} for booking {{5}}. Please arrange payment at your earliest convenience. — Samana Builders & Developers
templates.notes: No late-fee wording by business decision.

templates.body: Dear {{1}}, installment #{{2}} of Rs {{3}} was due on {{4}} and is now overdue for booking {{5}}. Total outstanding: Rs {{6}}. Please arrange payment at your earliest convenience. — Samana Builders & Developers
templates.notes: No late_fee parameter — the business does not charge late fees.

templates.body: Dear {{1}}, your receipt {{2}} has been generated for Rs {{3}} dated {{4}}. Payment ID: {{5}}. — Samana Builders & Developers

not_a_template.notes: The staff manual-send view composes arbitrary text, so it cannot use a template. Meta only allows free-form text within 24h of the customer's last message; outside that window it fails with 131047. The UI warns about this.
